name: Databricks
summary: Databricks builds the data-and-AI layer enterprises use to prepare data, run analytics, and deploy AI applications.
overview: Databricks is a San Francisco-based data and AI company founded by the creators of Apache Spark.

facts.label: Latest financing
facts.note: Closed August 2026 at a reported $190B valuation.

bull_case: Data and AI workloads sit at the center of enterprise software budgets.
bear_case: Cloud competition and AI infrastructure spending can pressure growth and margins.

intelligence.description: Databricks sells a unified platform for data engineering, analytics, machine learning, and enterprise AI. Its strategic question is whether the lakehouse becomes the system of record for the data and context AI agents need.
company: Databricks was founded by the team behind Apache Spark and built its business around the lakehouse: an architecture combining data-lake flexibility with the governance and performance associated with data warehouses. It is sold across the major clouds for data engineering, business intelligence, machine learning, and AI workloads.

The company is moving beyond storage and analytics into the application layer. Its current product push includes Lakebase, a managed database for AI-built applications, Unity AI Gateway for controlling model access and spend, and Genie for querying enterprise information through natural language.
intelligence.why_it_matters: Databricks is one of the clearest private-market tests of whether enterprise AI spend consolidates around a data platform rather than a single model provider. Its scale makes it a consequential future public-market comparable for Snowflake, cloud platforms, and AI infrastructure vendors.

changed.text: Acquired MosaicML, expanding from data tooling toward foundation-model and generative-AI workloads.
Announced a $10B Series J investment at a $62B valuation.
Raised capital at a reported $100B valuation as investor attention shifted to enterprise AI infrastructure.
A financing reportedly placed Databricks at $134B.
Closed a $5B strategic round at $190B and reported revenue run-rate above $7B.

takeaways: The valuation rests on proving its data platform is central to enterprise AI deployment, not merely analytics.
A $7B-plus run-rate gives Databricks unusual scale for a private software company.
Lakebase, Genie, and Unity AI Gateway move it closer to workflows where AI value is captured.
Risks include premium valuation, cloud-platform dependency, and competition from Snowflake, hyperscalers, and specialists.
